---
title: "J: Antiinfectives for systemic use"
description: "ATC group J for modellers: exposure indices referenced to a pathogen MIC, growth and kill models carrying resistant subpopulations, and viral dynamics."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

Drugs given systemically against an invading organism, bacteria, fungi, mycobacteria and viruses, plus immune sera and vaccines under the same letter [@whoccATCDDDIndex2026].
The potency term is a property of the pathogen isolate, its MIC, rather than of the patient (see [PKPD](/docs/modeling/pkpd/)) [@moutonStandardizationPharmacokineticPharmacodynamic2005].

Fleming's mould plate of 1928 became a medicine only in February 1941, when Florey's Oxford group treated a constable, Albert Alexander [@sheppardShortcourseAntibioticTherapy2022; @barrettLegacyPenicillinFirst2023].
He responded, but penicillin re-purified from his urine was not enough to keep the course going, the supply ran out and he died [@sheppardShortcourseAntibioticTherapy2022; @gaynesDiscoveryPenicillinNew2017].
Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the 1945 Nobel Prize [@gaynesDiscoveryPenicillinNew2017].

| Level 2 code | Description |
| ---: | :--- |
| J01 | Antibacterials for systemic use |
| J02 | Antimycotics for systemic use |
| J04 | Antimycobacterials |
| J05 | Antivirals for systemic use |
| J06 | Immune sera and immunoglobulins |
| J07 | Vaccines |

## Modelling notes

**Endpoint.**
For antibacterials it is bacterial count, log CFU, from time-kill or animal infection experiments [@craigPharmacokineticPharmacodynamicParameters1998; @nielsenSemimechanisticPharmacokineticPharmacodynamic2007].
For J05 it is plasma viral load [@perelsonHIV1DynamicsVivo1996; @neumannHepatitisCViral1998].

**The index is class-specific.**
For antibacterials, exposure is summarised as **unbound** concentration referenced to the **MIC**: *f*T~>MIC~, *f*AUC/MIC or *f*C~max~/MIC [@moutonStandardizationPharmacokineticPharmacodynamic2005].
Which index predicts effect is settled by dose fractionation and differs between antibacterial classes, so no single index covers J01 [@craigPharmacokineticPharmacodynamicParameters1998; @nielsenPharmacokineticPharmacodynamicModelingAntibacterial2013].

**Typical structure.**
Semi-mechanistic models give the bacteria a growth rate, a capacity limit and a drug-driven kill rate, fitted to whole time-kill curves rather than one summary index [@nielsenSemimechanisticPharmacokineticPharmacodynamic2007].

**Resistance is a compartment.**
Regrowth is usually modelled as a pre-existing less susceptible subpopulation that treatment selects for, though published models differ in how resistance arises [@jumbeApplicationMathematicalModel2003; @nielsenPharmacokineticPharmacodynamicModelingAntibacterial2013].

**J05 models the host too.**
The hepatitis C model carries uninfected cells, infected cells and virions, with interferon entering as a fractional block of virion production [@neumannHepatitisCViral1998].
Under a protease inhibitor, HIV load decay gave short lifespans for productively infected cells and virions [@perelsonHIV1DynamicsVivo1996].

**Easy to overlook.**
MIC is a discrete two-fold scale carrying real measurement error [@moutonVariationMICMeasurements2018].
Unbound concentration is the active one, yet there is no standard way to account for protein binding in *in vitro* pharmacodynamic testing [@zeitlingerProteinBindingDo2011].
After hepatitis A vaccination, antibody titres decay multiphasically, set by the lifespans of antibody and of short- and long-lived plasma cells [@andraudLivingThreeTime2012].

**Mechanistic extrapolation.**
PBPK has been applied to antiretrovirals where trials are hard: exposure in pregnancy [@desousamendesPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2015] and release from long-acting intramuscular depots [@bettonteDevelopmentPhysiologicallyBased2024].
For J04 the hollow fibre system is qualified by the EMA as a methodology supporting the development of antituberculosis regimens [@cavaleriHollowFiberSystem2015].
